places.title: Edificio Mirador
places.why: A social housing block with a giant opening: a communal garden about 37 m up frames the Sierra de Guadarrama, while nine stacked blocks each get their own facade. Residential — view it from outside.

places.title: PAU de Carabanchel
places.architect: Foreign Office Architects, dosmasuno, Amann-Cánovas-Maruri, Morphosis, José Cruz Ovalle and others
places.area: Metro L11 La Peseta / Carabanchel Alto
places.why: Madrid's densest cluster of experimental public housing: a dozen blocks by Spanish and international studios within walking distance — bamboo shutters, colour-coded balconies, stacked white cubes.

places.title: Edificio Celosía
places.why: A lattice of stacked apartment blocks with voids cut through it, giving every home light, views and shared terraces instead of a closed courtyard. A few minutes on foot from the Mirador.

places.title: PAU Ensanche de Vallecas
places.architect: Ecosistema Urbano, Estudio Entresitio, Rueda & Pizarro, Núñez Ribot, Guillermo Vázquez Consuegra
places.area: Metro L1 La Gavia / Las Suertes
places.why: Madrid's other large laboratory of public housing. On the Ecobulevar, three cylindrical air trees by Ecosistema Urbano shade and cool the street while the new trees grow.

places.title: Colonia El Viso
places.why: The most complete rationalist neighbourhood in Spain: 242 white cubic houses with gardens, built by a cooperative on quiet streets named after rivers. A green, calm place to walk.

places.title: Poblado dirigido de Caño Roto
places.architect: Antonio Vázquez de Castro, José Luis Íñiguez de Onzoño
places.why: A low-rise village of patio houses and small blocks built for rural migrants, one of the landmarks of Spanish post-war housing. The architects themselves lived here for a while.

places.title: Entrepatios Las Carolinas
places.why: Madrid's first ecological cohousing: 17 flats and shared spaces in a timber building, owned by a cooperative whose residents hold rights of use.

places.title: EMVS public housing, Puente de Vallecas
places.architect: Marmolbravo + MADhel (NSA6 LaScalA, NSA13 Twpeaks, SFJ6); Ricardo Sánchez González + Ángel Munárriz (NSA14)
places.why: The newest generation of municipal housing around Calle Peña Falconera: serpentine and stepped blocks with pedestrian passages and stepped plazas. The Antonio Palacios Awards 2025 singled out Marmolbravo + MADhel's building at Peña Falconera 2.

places.title: 20 viviendas en Alcalá 141
places.why: Winner of the Antonio Palacios Awards 2025 for new buildings: a stone facade that nods to Antonio Palacios's Madrid over a warm oak base.

places.title: Ciudad BBVA / La Vela
places.why: The bank's headquarters as a low, garden-filled town of linear blocks with fixed louvres, crowned by La Vela, a 93 m elliptical tower.

places.title: Cuatro Torres Business Area
places.architect: Foster + Partners, Pelli Clarke Pelli, Pei Cobb Freed, Rubio & Álvarez-Sala, Fenwick Iribarren
places.why: Five skyscrapers on the former Real Madrid training grounds that redrew Madrid's skyline; visible from most of the city.

points.name: Torre de Cristal — Pelli Clarke Pelli

photos.author: M.Peinado from Alcalá de Henares, España
M.Peinado from Alcalá de Henares, España

places.title: CaixaForum Madrid
places.why: A brick power station lifted off the ground: its base was removed so the old walls float over a covered plaza, next to a vertical garden by Patrick Blanc.

places.title: Barajas Airport Terminal 4
places.why: An undulating roof on colour-graded steel trees over a bamboo-lined ceiling; Stirling Prize 2006. You will see it on arrival.

places.title: Madrid Río and the Arganzuela footbridge
places.architect: MRIO (Burgos & Garrido, Porras La Casta, Rubio & Álvarez-Sala) + West 8; bridge by Dominique Perrault
places.why: The M-30 ring road was buried in a tunnel and replaced by a riverside park several kilometres long, often cited by urbanists as a model. Perrault's bridge is two steel spirals over the park and the river.

places.why: Three new volumes gathered under one red roof that cantilevers up to 36 m, with an open courtyard between them.

places.title: Museo ABC
places.why: A former Mahou brewery turned drawing museum: the courtyard became the atrium, and the new street facade is a lattice of perforated triangular steel.

places.title: Edificio Castelar
places.architect: Rafael de La-Hoz Arderius, Gerardo Olivares
places.why: A glass prism that seems to hover above its travertine base — one of the boldest office buildings of 1980s Madrid.

places.title: Norman Foster Foundation
places.architect: Foster + Partners (pavilion); mansion by Joaquín Saldaña, 1912
places.why: Foster's foundation in an early-20th-century mansion: archive, library and a glass pavilion in the garden.

places.title: Hipódromo de la Zarzuela
places.architect: Carlos Arniches, Martín Domínguez, Eduardo Torroja
places.why: Torroja's thin concrete shells cantilever about 13 m over the grandstands and are only a few centimetres thick at the edge — a classic of structural architecture.

places.title: Parroquia de Santa Mónica
places.why: Church, parish rooms and housing folded into one sculptural volume clad in weathering steel and lit by clusters of skylights.

places.title: Fundación Giner de los Ríos
places.architect: amid.cero9 (Cristina Díaz Moreno, Efrén García Grinda)
places.why: The historic home of the Institución Libre de Enseñanza, extended with pavilions wrapped in steel rods and climbing plants around a sunken garden.

places.title: Biblioteca de los Mil Soles (Francisco Umbral)
places.why: A public library filled with daylight from rows of skylights and louvres, with the street in front turned over to pedestrians.

places.title: Torres Blancas
places.why: An organic concrete tower that grows like a tree, with round terraces clustered around its cores; one of the key Spanish buildings of the 20th century. Residential — view it from outside.

places.title: Instituto del Patrimonio Cultural de España (Crown of Thorns)
places.area: Ciudad Universitaria, Calle del Pintor El Greco 4
places.why: A circular concrete building ringed by a jagged crown of beams, known as the Crown of Thorns; protected as a Site of Cultural Interest since 2001.

places.title: CEDEX — Centro de Estudios Hidrográficos
places.why: A laboratory hall spanned by Fisac's hollow, post-tensioned concrete bone beams — an engineering experiment that became architecture.

places.title: Parroquia de Santa Ana y la Esperanza
places.why: A concrete church with Fisac's wave-shaped eaves and a slim bell tower, lit from above.

places.title: Castellana 81 (BBVA Tower)
places.why: The former Banco de Bilbao tower: groups of floors hung from two concrete cores behind a dark facade of weathering steel and bronze glass.

places.title: Nuestra Señora del Rosario de Filipinas
places.area: Salamanca, Calle del Conde de Peñalver 40
places.why: A brutalist church inserted into a street of bourgeois apartment blocks: heavy raw-concrete volumes and a monumental entrance porch.

places.why: Two office towers leaning 15° towards each other across Plaza de Castilla — the first inclined skyscrapers in the world.

M.Peinado from Alcalá de Henares, España

places.why: Higueras's garden housing block: stepped concrete terraces overgrown with climbing plants.

places.title: Edificio Los Cubos
places.architect: Michel Andrault, Pierre Parat, Aydin Guvan, Alain Capieu
places.area: Calle de Albacete 5, by the M-30
places.why: An office tower of glass cubes stacked around concrete pillars — a brutalist sculpture at the entrance to the city.

places.title: Torre de Valencia
places.area: Calle de O'Donnell 4, by the Retiro
places.why: A brutalist residential tower in textured concrete at the edge of the Retiro park.

places.title: Edificio Beatriz
places.area: Calle de José Ortega y Gasset
places.why: A brutalist office block in the Salamanca district, its long facades ribbed with deep vertical fins.

places.title: UGT Madrid headquarters
places.why: A stepped concrete tower with a coffered underside, 250 m from Torres Blancas — worth seeing together.

places.title: Pabellón de los Hexágonos
places.architect: José Antonio Corrales, Ramón Vázquez Molezún
places.why: Spain's pavilion for Expo 58 in Brussels, built from hexagonal umbrella modules and later rebuilt in the Casa de Campo.

places.title: Museo del Prado
places.architect: Juan de Villanueva; extension by Rafael Moneo (2007)
places.why: Villanueva's neoclassical museum of natural science turned into one of the first public art museums; Moneo's brick cube around the cloister of the Jerónimos adds the new galleries.

places.title: Parque del Retiro
places.architect: Royal park of the Buen Retiro palace; Palacio de Cristal by Ricardo Velázquez Bosco (1887)
places.why: The former royal park at the heart of the city: a grand pond with a colonnade, formal avenues and gardens, and the glass-and-iron Palacio de Cristal by a small lake.

places.title: Paseo del Prado, Cibeles and Puerta de Alcalá
places.architect: José de Hermosilla (Salón del Prado); Francesco Sabatini (Puerta de Alcalá)
places.why: The 18th-century tree-lined promenade of fountains and museums — the Landscape of Light — from the Cibeles fountain to Atocha, with Sabatini's triumphal gate at the corner of the Retiro.

places.title: Royal Palace and Almudena Cathedral
places.why: The vast granite and limestone royal palace on the edge of the ridge above the Manzanares, facing the cathedral across the Plaza de la Armería.

places.title: Plaza Mayor
places.architect: Juan Gómez de Mora; rebuilt by Juan de Villanueva
places.why: An enclosed arcaded square of red facades and slate-roofed towers, the stage of the old city's markets, festivals and executions.

places.title: Puerta del Sol
places.architect: Real Casa de Correos by Jaime Marquet
places.why: The half-moon square at the centre of Madrid and of Spain’s road network, faced by the old Post Office with its clock tower.

photos.file: 126 Puerta del Sol (Madrid), al fons la Real Casa de Correos, seu de la Comunidad de Madrid.jpg
photos.author: Enric

places.title: Gran Vía and the Metrópolis Building
places.why: The early 20th-century boulevard cut through the old town, lined with theatres, cinemas and the first skyscrapers of Madrid, starting at the domed Metrópolis Building.

places.title: Temple of Debod
places.architect: Ancient Egyptian temple, rebuilt in Madrid
places.why: A Nubian temple given to Spain and rebuilt stone by stone on a hill above the Manzanares, in a reflecting pool facing the sunset.

places.title: Museo Thyssen-Bornemisza (Palacio de Villahermosa)
places.why: A neoclassical palace on the Paseo del Prado turned into a museum by Moneo, with top-lit rooms around a central hall.

photos.file: Site of the Retiro and the Prado in Madrid 49 (29684554308).jpg
photos.author: Kyle Magnuson from Los Angeles, United States

places.title: Galería de las Colecciones Reales
places.why: A granite museum built into the slope below the Royal Palace: long galleries behind a colonnade of stone fins, with views over the Campo del Moro.

photos.file: Fachada oeste de la Catedral de la Almudena, Madrid, España 01.jpg
photos.author: Riozujar

places.title: Real Jardín Botánico
places.why: An 18th-century botanical garden on three terraces next to the Prado, with glasshouses and thousands of plant species.

places.title: Campo del Moro
places.why: The palace's English-style landscape garden on the slope down to the Manzanares, with a long lawn that frames the west facade of the Royal Palace.

places.title: Jardines de Sabatini
places.why: Formal neoclassical gardens of clipped hedges and a long pond on the north side of the Royal Palace.

places.title: Casa de Campo
places.why: Madrid's largest green space: pine woods, a lake with a view of the skyline and trails across a former royal estate.

places.title: Jardines de las Vistillas
places.why: Terraced gardens on the edge of the old town, with sunset views over the Manzanares valley and the Sierra.

places.title: El Capricho de la Alameda de Osuna
places.architect: Jean-Baptiste Mulot, for the Duchess of Osuna
places.why: A romantic garden of the Enlightenment with a hedge maze, a small palace, a hermitage, temples and ponds — French, English and Italian gardens in one.

places.title: Quinta de la Fuente del Berro
places.why: A hidden landscaped garden on several levels with winding paths, stone stairs, ponds and peacocks, close to the city centre.

places.title: Jardín del Príncipe de Anglona
places.why: A small walled palace garden of the 18th century behind the Plaza de la Paja, with geometric box hedges and a quiet fountain.

places.why: A hillside landscape park with shaded paths, a stream and a rose garden, running down from the Temple of Debod toward the river.

places.title: Quinta de Torre Arias
places.why: A former aristocratic country estate with an old palace, meadows, cedars and olive groves, opened to the public only recently.

places.title: Parque del Cerro del Tío Pío
places.why: Grassy round hills made from old rubble in Vallecas, with one of the widest open views over the Madrid skyline — a local sunset spot.

places.title: Quinta de los Molinos
places.why: A former country estate with almond groves that blossom pink and white in February and March, olive trees, ponds and two old windmills.

places.architect: Emilio Esteras, José Luis Esteban Penelas
places.why: A large contemporary park of olive groves, water channels and open-air sculptures, laid out around a ring for the 1992 Cultural Capital year.
